settings.name_in_paper: Lipschitz MAB problem (standard Lipschitz MAB problem)
unmapped: metric space (L,X) of diameter <= 1 is revealed to the learner, accessed via a covering oracle
Lipschitz constant 1 w.r.t. the given metric
settings.definition_quote: In the Lipschitz MAB problem on (L,X), there is a strategy set X, a metric space (L,X) of diameter <= 1, and a payoff function mu : X -> [0,1] such that ... |mu(x)-mu(y)| <= L(x,y) ... The metric space (L,X) is revealed to an algorithm, whereas the payoff function mu is not. In each round the algorithm chooses a strategy x in X and observes an independent random sample from a payoff distribution D(x) with support S subset [0,1] and expectation mu(x).

settings.name_in_paper: Noisy Lipschitz MAB problem with normal noise
unmapped: metric space revealed to learner via covering oracle
noise distribution revealed to the algorithm
settings.definition_quote: The Noisy Lipschitz MAB problem is a standard Lipschitz MAB problem such that every time any strategy u is played, the reward is mu(u) plus an independent random sample from some fixed distribution P (called the noise distribution) which is revealed to the algorithm.

settings.name_in_paper: Lipschitz MAB with heavy-tailed reward distributions (bounded absolute third moment)
unmapped: rewards independent but not necessarily identically distributed across trials of the same strategy, with mean mu(v)
bounded absolute third moment E|X|^3 < rho
settings.definition_quote: it suffices to assume that X_n(v) is an independent random variable with mean mu(v) in [0,1] and a uniformly bounded bounded absolute third moment. Note that different trials of the same strategy {X_n(v)} do not need to be identically distributed.

unmapped: payoff function mu(u) = 1 - L(u,S) (or f(L(u,S)) for a shape function) for an unknown target set S
settings.definition_quote: The Target MAB problem on a metric space (L,X) with a target set S subset X is the standard Lipschitz MAB problem on (L,X) with payoff function mu(u) = 1-L(u,S).

symbols.C_z: constant C in the C-zooming dimension (any C>0)
symbols.d_z: C-zooming dimension of the problem instance

source.label: thm:zooming-dim
source.quote: Consider the \standardMAB. Let \A\ be Algorithm~\ref{alg:nice-1d}. Then $\forall\,C>0$ R_\A(t) \leq O(C \log t)^{1/(2+d)}\,\times t^{1-1/(2+d)} for all $t$, where $d$ is the $C$-zooming dimension of the problem instance.

results.notes: Regret defined as t*mu* minus expected payoff, i.e. pseudo-regret. Holds for all C>0 simultaneously; algorithm not parameterized by C. Compute: uses one covering-oracle call per round. Theorem 1.3 is the informal version.

symbols.d_cov: covering dimension of the metric space (c-covering dimension in the proof)

conditions: metric space has covering dimension d_cov

source.label: lm:naive-alg
source.quote: Consider the Lipschitz MAB problem on a metric space $(L,X)$ of covering dimension $d$. Let \A\ be the na\"ive algorithm that uses $\textsc{ucb1}$ in each phase. Then $\RegretDim(\A)\leq d$.

results.notes: Statement is RegretDim(A) <= d; the proof shows R(t) = O~(t^{(d+1)/(d+2)}) assuming d is a c-covering dimension (constant depends on c). Paper attributes the technique to Kleinberg 2004, so marked not new.

bound.regime: for every eps_alg>0, for infinitely many t on some instance (regret not O(t^gamma) for any gamma < (d+1)/(d+2))

symbols.d_mm: max-min-covering dimension MaxMinCOV(X) of the metric space

source.label: thm:mincov-lb
source.quote: If $X$ is a metric space and $d$ is the max-min-covering dimension of $X$ then $\RegretDim(\A) \geq d$ for every bandit algorithm $\A$.

results.notes: Statement in terms of regret dimension; proof shows for any gamma<(d+1)/(d+2) and constant C, Pr_{mu,A}(forall t R_A(t) < C t^gamma) = 0 under a random needle-in-haystack instance distribution (Bernoulli rewards). Encoded as Omega(T^{gamma}) holding infinitely often; this is a liminf-type exponent lower bound, not a finite-time bound. Lower half of Theorem 1.2.

bound.regime: for all t >= t_0, where t_0 depends on the instance; any d_alg > d_fat

symbols.d_alg: target dimension d > d* used by the algorithm
symbols.d_fat: d* such that the metric has a d*-fat decomposition

conditions: compact metric space with a d*-fat decomposition D of finite depth

source.label: thm:fatness
source.quote: Consider the Lipschitz MAB problem on a fixed compact metric space with a $d^*$-fat decomposition $\mathcal{D}$. Then for any $d>d^*$ there is an algorithm $\A_\mathcal{D}$ such that $\RegretDim(\A_\mathcal{D}) \leq d$.

results.notes: RegretDim <= d means for every instance and every d'>d, R(t) <= t^{1-1/(d'+2)} for large t; expression records the definition with target dimension.

bound.regime: for all t >= t_0 (instance-dependent); any d_alg > MaxMinCOV(X)

conditions: access to depth oracle and D-covering oracle for a transfinite fat decomposition

source.label: thm:PMO
source.quote: Consider the Lipschitz MAB problem on a compact metric space $(L,X)$. For any $d>\MaxMinCOV(X)$ there exists an algorithm $\A_d$ such that $\RegretDim(\A_d) \leq d$.

results.notes: Together with Theorem 3.7 gives Theorem 1.2: R_A(t)=O_I(t^gamma) for any gamma>(d+1)/(d+2), d=MaxMinCOV(X). Regret dimension is an asymptotic notion.

source.label: thm:zooming-dim-generalized
source.quote: Consider an instance of the \standardMAB\ for which there exists a $(\beta, c_0)$-good confidence radius, $\beta\geq 0$. ... (a) If $d+\beta>1$ then $R_\A(t) \leq a(t)\; t^{1-1/(d+\beta)}$ for all $t$, where $a(t) = O(c\,c_0\,\log^2 t)^{1/(d+\beta)}$.

results.notes: Applies to noisy variants via Corollaries 4.5/4.6 (point-mass noise, peaked/jump densities) which only establish good confidence radii.

results.notes: Expression is Theorem 2.4's bound times sigma, as stated.

source.label: thm:zooming-dim-maxReward
source.quote: Consider the \standardMAB. There is an algorithm \A\ which is $2$-good in general, and $1$-good when the maximal expected reward is $1$.

results.notes: Derived by instantiating 'beta-good' (Definition 4.7, properties (a),(b) of Theorem 4.2) with beta=2; c_0 is an absolute constant. Since d+2>1 always, only case (a) applies.

source.label: thm:targetMAB
source.quote: Consider the Target MAB problem on a metric space of finite doubling dimension $d^*$. Let \A\ be the zooming algorithm from Theorem~\ref{thm:zooming-dim-maxReward}. Then R_{\A}(t) \leq (c\, 2^{O(d^*)}\log^2 t)\; t^{1-1/(1+d)} for all $t$, where $d$ is the $c$-covering dimension of the target set $S$.

results.notes: Poly-logarithmic if S finite (d=0). Extension stated in passing for Y not containing S gives t^{1-1/(2+d)}.

source.label: thm:targetMAB-shape
source.quote: Consider the Target MAB problem on a metric space $(L,X)$ of finite doubling dimension $d^*$, with shape function $f(x) = x^{1/\alpha}$, $\alpha>0$. Let \A\ be the zooming algorithm on $(L_f,X)$. Then R_{\A}(t) \leq (c\, 2^{O(d^*)}\log^2 t)\; t^{1-1/(1+\alpha d)} for all $t$, where $d$ is the $c$-covering dimension of the target set $S$.

results.notes: Paper's mu with shape function is stated as f(L(u,S)); setting definition uses 1-L(u,S); the shape-function form slightly differs.

source.label: thm:zooming-dim-BerryEsseen
source.quote: Assume that each $X_n(v)$ is an independent random variable with mean $\mu(v)\in [0,1]$ and furthermore that $ E\left[\,|X_n(v)|^3\,\right] < \rho$ for some constant $\rho$. Then there is an algorithm \A\ such that if for some $c$ the problem instance has $c$-zooming dimension $d$ then R_\A(t) \leq a(t)\; t^{1-1/(3d+6)} for all $t$, where $a(t) = O(c \rho \log t)^{1/(3d+6)}$.

results.notes: Proof only sketched. Unclear whether algorithm needs rho.
